answer: A per-credential bond is the Sybil brake. Minting a credential needs a locked stake, and each stake backs one identity only, so n fakes cost n bonds. Emission is pooled and fixed, so every new credential dilutes the share of all others: an attacker paying n bonds earns what one honest agent earns. Marginal cost rises while revenue stays flat, so each extra fake account deepens the loss. Exit friction adds an unbonding delay and a burned fee, so cycling identities to farm epoch bonuses destroys value. Each fake relic of trust, copper of stake, and seat in the shared grove is paid separately.
